h: The Inaugural Offerings Repair Sin at Its Root

p: You have something on your hands at the beginning,
and you have something on your hands at the end;
and you have something on your hands at the end:
עָשׂוּ לָהֶם עֵגֶל מַסֵּכָה (שְׁמוֹת לב, ח)
and atone for the deed of the goats,
and atone for the deed of the calf."
the connection of "and they slaughtered a goat" to the calf,
that these are called beginning and end.
Yisrael did not take a calf
and the calf for a chatas Aharon offered;
so what is this that it says,
"Let a calf come and atone," etc.?
"'And an ox and a ram for shelamim' (Vayikra 9:4)
because the sin was likened to two species,
as it says, 'they made themselves a molten calf,'
for the likeness of an ox that eats grass.'
and atone for the deed of the ox;
and atone for the deed of the calf."
הָא יִשְׂרָאֵל לֹא עָשׂוּ רַק עֵגֶל
after all, Yisrael made only a calf
so why is the sin likened to an ox?
Also further on in Toras Kohanim (8) it is stated:
in the likeness of an ox,
why it appeared to him in the likeness of an ox
and not in the likeness of a calf.
as is stated in Toras Kohanim (9):
וַיַּקְרֵב אֵת קָרְבַּן הָעָם (וַיִּקְרָא ט, טו)
once he had finished with his own offerings,
he went on to the people's offering.
does not atone for the Kohanim,
for himself and for the people,
'and atone for yourself and for the people.'"
הָא הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת הָיוּ עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל
after all, the offerings were for all Yisrael,
so why were the Kohanim not atoned for through them?
But in truth it is written (Shemos 32:21):
"What did this people do to you,
that you have brought a great sin upon it?"
is said of an unintentional sin
אַךְ בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (צַו, וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה י, ג) אִיתָא
But in the Midrash Rabbah (Tzav, Vayikra Rabbah 10:3) it is stated:
Better that the offense be ascribed to me
Yisrael could ascribe it to Aharon,
and for them it was unintentional;
were punished with death by dropsy
And those who mainly needed atonement
were those who went somewhat astray
"that you have brought a great sin upon it"
that is, the sin of idolatry.
although the yetzer hara had returned to its place,
as in the years of Hevel,
when there was no idolatry in the world,
to uproot the yetzer hara completely.
And once he brought upon them
then there is no longer any way
to uproot the yetzer hara completely,
except when everything will be rectified
and Hashem Yisbarach will slaughter the yetzer hara.
And this is what is said, "a great sin."
the main rectification was required of Aharon,
and he was commanded to bring a calf as a chatas
to atone for the deed of the calf;
and consequently he atoned for himself and for the people.
For if there had been no atonement for Yisrael,
there would still be a claim against him:
"that you have brought a great sin upon it."
And Yisrael needed only a calf as an olah,
for an olah is a gift
And this is what Toras Kohanim asks:
only a chatas and an olah.
"You have something on your hands at the beginning," etc.
For the matter of "and they slaughtered a goat"
that Yosef was liable to death
or to be sold as a slave.
But through this it came about
that they went down to Egypt
and came to the sin of idolatry,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ב, ח)
וְזוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב קע, ב)
וְאַחַר כָּךְ הָיָה בֶּאֱמֶת גָּלוּת מִצְרַיִם
And afterward the Egyptian exile truly was
a preparation for the Giving of the Torah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ה׳ סוֹף עַמּוּד א)
as they said (Berachos 5a, end of the amud).
And this is what it says:
"You have something on your hands at the beginning,"
"and you have something on your hands at the end,"
and this too was an unintentional sin.
And for the sin of the calf
the calf of Aharon's chatas atoned,
and for the unintentional sin of the goat
they brought a goat as a chatas.
And this is what it says:
and atone for the deed of the goats."
But a gift was still needed to appease,
so that their heart should be in holiness;
and for this the calf came as an olah.
Now we find in the Gemara (Chagigah 13b):
וְאִלּוּ שׁוֹר לָא קָא חָשֵׁיב כוּ׳
"Yet the ox it does not count," etc.;
and He turned it into a keruv," etc.;
is the same as the face of a man
a large face and a small face."
the Vav, the Holy One, blessed be He,
and opposite these there are in the kelipah
the kelipah of the ox, the large face,
and the kelipah of the calf, the small face.
had on their hands an unintentional sin,
in that they made a molten calf;
to uproot all of Yisrael's faith
and this is what is said, "And they exchanged their Glory"
"for the likeness of an ox that eats grass,"
the ox of the kelipah, the large face.
And this is what is said (Tehillim 106:19):
and bowed down to a molten image"
that is what is said in the Torah,
for the likeness of an ox," etc.
that is according to the intention of the erev rav.
And this is what it says:
לְפִי שֶׁנִּדְמֵית עֲבֵירָה לְב׳ מִינִים כוּ׳
"because the sin was likened to two species," etc.,
and atone for the deed of the ox;
and atone for the deed of the calf."
That is, after they brought a calf as an olah
to atone for the sin of the calf
עַל יְדֵי עֵגֶל לְחַטָּאת שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן
through Aharon's calf as a chatas,
and needing the calf as an olah
through which they merited the abundant wisdom
which they merited with the second Tablets
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה תִּשָּׂא פָּרָשָׁה מו, מז)
(as stated in Midrash Rabbah, Ki Sisa, ch. 46-47)
they brought an ox as shelamim.
so that one can eat of sacred offerings;
as they merited after the tenth plague,
when they had, for the moment,
they merited eating the Pesach offering;
that they rectified the root of the serpent's blemish,
And this "atones for the deed of the ox,"
which was a sin at the root,
according to the intention of the erev rav:
"And they exchanged their Glory for the likeness of an ox"
the Arich Anpin of the kelipah.
And this atonement Aharon did not need,
for since he offered his calf as a chatas,
he already merited eating in holiness,
for the Kohanim eat of the flesh of the chatas.
And this is what it says (Toras Kohanim 9):
which came to atone for the deed of the ox,
does not atone for the Kohanim,
for the Kohanim eat even of a chatas,
וְנִתְקַן עַל יְדֵי עֵגֶל לְחַטָּאת שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן
and it was rectified through Aharon's calf as a chatas;
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן קָרְבָּנוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן
which is not so with Aharon's offering,
which atones for himself and for the people;
for they did not bring at all
only a calf as an olah,
for the atonement of the unintentional sin was completed
עַל יְדֵי עֵגֶל לְחַטָּאת שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן
through Aharon's calf as a chatas;
there would still be a claim
עַל אַהֲרֹן קְדוֹשׁ ה׳ (תְּהִלִּים קו, טז)
against Aharon, "the holy one of Hashem" (Tehillim 106:16):
"that you have brought a great sin upon it."
And this is what it says (Toras Kohanim 8):
in the likeness of an ox,
and was afraid of it," etc.;
that is, there was ascribed to him
also the root of the blemish,
which was the deed of the erev rav.
"My brother, of this you are afraid?
for through this you will be elevated,
for you were chosen to be the atoning Kohen,
to rectify everything at its root,
וַיֵּרָא כְבוֹד ה׳ אֶל כָּל הָעָם (וַיִּקְרָא ט, כג)
"And the glory of Hashem appeared to all the people" (Vayikra 9:23):
and they will merit to see the new fire,
when He will uproot all the yetzer hara from their heart,
when they will merit the upper Shabbos,
from which the yetzer hara has cleared away.
